frontier.hypothesis: The deciding input is OUTSIDE the function body, in the TRANSLATION-UNIT context - the math_Distance3D prototype, the position of func_80017848 within src/ings.c, or the number/order of the file's preceding declarations. This is the only named axis in thirteen sessions that has never been probed, and it is now the highest-yield remaining item because s11/s12 closed every in-body structural region by hand and s13 closed the same space by machine.
frontier.mechanism: GCC 2.7.2's allocno ordering (local-alloc's reg_n_refs / live-length inputs) and cse's hash tables are affected by state that accumulates across the whole translation unit, not just the function - cf. the cc1-first-pass-scheduler-bug memory, where ~1400 lines of preceding declarations changed cc1's behaviour on a trivial function. The declared prototype of math_Distance3D additionally decides how its two arguments are set up, and therefore the register pressure of the tail that feeds back into loop 2's preheader tie. Nothing inside the function body can move any of that.
frontier.next_probe: Sweep the TU rather than the function, re-scoring each cell with tmp/grind/func_80017848/s13/score.sh: (a) the math_Distance3D prototype in the header - s32* vs void* vs a struct pointer, 2 args vs 3, and whether the call-site arguments are cast; (b) the position of func_80017848 within src/ings.c relative to its neighbours (move it above/below the adjacent functions); (c) the presence and order of the file's preceding declarations. SCOPE CONSTRAINT: only src/ings.c and include/ headers are touchable - do NOT touch the Makefile, the linker script or the pipeline txt files.

frontier.hypothesis: Target's loop-2 preheader copy is emitted by a pass that runs AFTER cse and combine - loop.c's strength-reduction preheader emission (emit_iv_add_mult) or regmove.c - and is therefore not producible by any C-level construct at all, which is why 47 + 23 hand cells and ~98k machine iterations all agree on a flat floor.
frontier.mechanism: Both of target's preheaders end with `addu v0,a0,v1` (the strength-reduced giv init for `base + i`), which is loop.c output emitted into the preheader after cse/combine have run. If loop.c or regmove.c materialises the `addu a3,a0,zero` copy, the deciding input is the loop's giv/biv structure rather than any addend expression - exactly the invariance s11, s12 and now s13 all measured. s13 strengthens the case: a randomizer that mutated the preheader jointly with every other region for 27,827 iterations never produced the copy either.
frontier.next_probe: Generate the full -da dump series for chassis A (score 3) using the re-pathed tmp/grind/func_80017848/s10/dump.sh and walk the loop-2 preheader insn stream ACROSS passes: .cse -> .loop -> .combine -> .lreg -> .greg. Identify at which dump the `addu a3,a0,zero`-shaped copy would have to appear, and in the .loop dump compare loop 1's and loop 2's giv/biv records side by side - they differ in OUTCOME inside a single dump, so the deciding record is directly visible. Do NOT re-probe any preheader addend spelling, declaration order, parameter homing, loop-body spelling, exit form, loop shape, or the base-destination local: all measured dead by s11/s12, and now by machine search in s13.
